issues.reason: The open-redirect guard keeps only the parsed path, but inputs like `////evil.com` (whose path parses as `//evil.com`) or `/\evil.com` give a protocol-relative or backslash path that browsers treat as an external host, so the user is redirected off-site after OAuth login.

The URL is fetched with `sync_client.stream` and `follow_redirects=True`, with no host or IP validation, so an attacker-supplied URL can make the server request internal or cloud-metadata addresses, and the response is saved to a file the attacker may be able to retrieve.

The request-body `hash` is inserted into `vibe_edit_history_dir / f"{hash}.py"` with no sanitization, so `../` sequences or an absolute path let an attacker open any `.py` file on the server and copy its contents into the watched demo file.
